correctness.rationale: On the positive half-plane the first coordinate obeys an exact second-order recurrence until its first nonpositive value, after which two further iterates give precisely the origin. For \(T^2<4D\), a sine-phase argument bounds every first exit by \(m=\lceil\pi/\arccos(T/(2\sqrt D))\rceil\); an explicit phase witness first vanishes at \(m+2\), proving minimality. The repeated-root and distinct-root closed forms give the exact extinction formula and persistent cone with switching boundaries included. Rational trajectory tests from the actual standalone script passed, but the infinite claims are analytic, not inferred from tests.

value.rationale: The exact unforced slice is a structurally natural bifurcation boundary explicitly singled out by the model introducers. It exhibits a genuine dichotomy: uniform finite-step annihilation for a complex-conjugate branch spectrum, versus a nonempty invariant strict-positive cone for real roots. The minimal extinction index has a sharp staircase with an inverse-square-root critical divergence. On the opposite side the complete persistent set and exact algebraic-versus-logarithmic settling-time crossover answer an all-initial-condition question not resolved by local eigenvalue stability or nonzero-forcing period tables. This is a natural full classification rather than an arbitrarily chosen finite computation.
